method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse replay of every implication in the complete-consistent-set proposition, direct checking of contradiction arguments against the imported derivability facts, and exact formula, macro, token, tag, label, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Complete consistent sets of sentences: definition, model-construction role, derivability closure, and membership conditions for conjunction, disjunction and conditional.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A sentence set Gamma is complete exactly when it contains A or not-A for every sentence A. A complete consistent extension Gamma-star decides each atomic case and thereby determines a structure or valuation whose truth induction requires the stated connective membership equivalences. The proof may silently use reflexivity, monotonicity and transitivity of derivability.
samples.checks: The title token, definition biconditional, consistency restriction, FOL/propositional construction branches, Gamma/Gamma-star containment and all imported section references are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For complete consistent Gamma, anything derivable from Gamma belongs to Gamma. Otherwise completeness puts its negation in Gamma, and derivability of A together with membership of not-A makes Gamma inconsistent.
samples.checks: All four proposition items retain their iff directions. The first proof uses completeness only to obtain not-A and the tagged explicit-inconsistency result to contradict consistency.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A conjunction belongs to Gamma iff both conjuncts do. Forward derivability gives each conjunct; backward derivability builds the conjunction; the first item converts each derived formula into membership.
samples.checks: The defAnd/probAnd guards, item numbers, four proof-system reference variants and both applications of prop:ccs-prov-in are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A disjunction belongs to Gamma iff at least one disjunct does. If neither belongs, completeness supplies both negations and the imported derivability result makes Gamma inconsistent; either member conversely derives the disjunction.
samples.checks: The contradiction direction, reverse direction, defOr/probOr guards, item numbers and disjunction formulas are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A conditional belongs to Gamma iff its antecedent is absent or its consequent is present. The forward contradiction uses modus-ponens-style derivability; the two reverse cases derive the conditional from not-A or from B. Separate tagged exercises ask for completion in FOL and propositional editions.
samples.checks: Both reverse cases remain separate, all membership negations and conditional directions are exact, proof-system reference order is preserved, and both indexed problem links retain their namespaces.

source_observations: The source alternates prose words complete and the controlled complete token; the translation preserves every controlled token occurrence while using संपूर्ण in surrounding Marathi.
The proof is parametric over four proof systems and two language tags; all tagrefs, item numbers and conditional proof guards remain exact.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, tags, labels, identifiers and reference options match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
संपूर्ण वाक्यसंच remains the definition-controlled specialist compound recorded in T192.
The one-sentence axiomatizable/decidable remark is paraphrased transparently from the frozen source and does not add a separate decision-procedure definition.
